settings.label: Roast chicken, Friday night
settings.answer:
Roast chicken wants grip and a little sweetness to meet the skin.

NON3 — toasted cinnamon, yuzu and orange pith, with enough grip to hold the fat. Serve it cold in a wine glass, not a tumbler.

If the bird comes with something green and bitter, pour NON1 alongside.

settings.label: Is this just grape juice?
settings.answer:
No. Nothing here is fermented and nothing is de-alcoholised.

Each bottle is cooked — ingredients toasted, reduced, salted, acidified — then blended for the structure alcohol used to provide. Tannin from tea and skins, salinity from kombu or salt, acid from citrus and vinegar.

It reads dry, not sweet. That surprises people.

settings.label: Off wine for a month
settings.answer:
Then you need the ritual intact: cold bottle, real glass, something to talk about.

Start with the Everyday Set — three bottles, three seats at the table: rosé, white, red. A month is roughly six bottles if you drink on weekends, so the mixed six is the cheaper way in.

settings.label: Gift for a chef
settings.answer:
Chefs taste for structure, so lead with NON2 — caramelised pear and kombu, savoury enough to be interesting on its own.

Put it in the Stopper Set so nothing is wasted between services. Seven days of carbonation, kept cold.
